judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures check out against the source, and the second one is exact. worksheet.tex problem 2 ends 'Explain in one line why the answer is not $9$'; problem 5(c) is 'In one sentence, say why the rounded value is not equal to $\sqrt{60}$'; problem 6 says 'State which table you used and why the square-root table is the wrong one here'; problem 7 says 'say which root you used and why an area leads to a square root rather than a cube root'; problem 11 says 'explain in one sentence why a volume calls for a cube root while an area calls for a square root'; problem 12(c) asks the student to judge a classmate's claim and 'explain what actually happens'. verify.json contains twelve entries, none of type manual, and machine_observation records gate_chain_manual_flags false — so all six explanation slots are inside a sheet the pipeline reports as fully machine-verified. The first hard failure also holds and is broader than the judge stated: problem 1 asks for the factor pair AND the root against one eval (12); problem 5(a) asks for the bracketing squares 49 and 64 and the whole numbers 7 and 8, which are exactly checkable and are not in verify.json; problem 12(a) asks the same for 64, 125, 4 and 5, also absent. The mathematics is not at issue: I recomputed 12, 3, 15, 7/8, 7.746->7.75, 7, 13, 2/5, sqrt(50)=7.0711<7.1, 0.6, 6 and 4.6416->4.64, and the study-guide try-its 11, 5, 0.7 and 9.4868->9.49, and all agree with both the key and verify.json. REJECT is correct.

strengths_to_preserve: The reference table at the top prints n, n^2 and n^3 for n = 1..15 with a stated caveat that 'No problem values are filled in --- use the numbers given in each problem'. It is a shared, value-free display, so it can never be mistaken for one problem's givens, and it is what makes problem 3 ($\sqrt{225}$, past the usual 12x12 table) solvable by factoring rather than guessing.

Problem 12 is the best-designed item on the sheet: $\sqrt[3]{100}$ is chosen because 100 is a perfect square but not a perfect cube, so the same radicand attacks the belief that a higher index gives a bigger root. The key answers it concretely -- '$\sqrt{100} = 10$ while $\sqrt[3]{100} \approx 4.64$' -- and generalises correctly: for n > 1, the higher the index the closer the root sits to 1.

64 is deliberately reused as the pivot in the study guide's Skill 2 example and again in its closing watch-out ('64 is in both lists, so $\sqrt{64} = 8$ while $\sqrt[3]{64} = 4$'). Naming the one radicand that appears in both tables is the cheapest way to force the student to read the index before the radicand.

The eight declared traps are all genuine student errors rather than arithmetic noise, and each is checkably distinct from the right answer: 144/2 = 72, 27/3 = 9, sqrt(343) = 18.52 for a cube root, cube-rooting the numerator only (0.016), and shifting the decimal point (0.06) for sqrt(0.36).

root_causes.description: The coverage rule is stated per PROBLEM, not per printed response slot, so a single eval discharges an item that asks for three separate written things. SKILL.md's JSON-format section requires only that 'every problem id 1..N has at least one check', and scripts/verify.py enforces exactly that at line ~2020. Every one of the twelve items here carries at least one check, so the gate chain reports the sheet green while six explanations and four bracketing values go unrecorded.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 5 prints three labelled parts (a)(b)(c); verify.json id 5 is a single approx (sqrt(60) -> 7.75) covering only (b)
worksheet.tex problem 12 prints three labelled parts (a)(b)(c); verify.json id 12 is a single approx (100**(1/3) -> 4.64) covering only (b)
worksheet.tex problem 1: 'Write the factor pair that produces $144$, then give the root' -- verify.json id 1 is one eval for the root
SKILL.md line 189: 'verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check'

root_causes.description: The author system knew the rule and argued its way around it. SKILL.md line 257 says 'Use manual for ... any explanation/reasoning answer', yet final_response.md writes 'Three problems also ask for a sentence of reasoning ... Those are teaching prose, not separate answers'. Two things are wrong there: six problems ask for reasoning, not three, and the sentence invents an exemption ('teaching prose') that the skill does not contain. Nothing in the pipeline contradicts the claim, so the rationalisation ships.

worksheet.tex: explanation clauses appear in problems 2, 5(c), 6, 7, 11 and 12(c) -- six, not three

root_causes.description: The Quick Answers bank blanks the one verified relation on the sheet. verify.json id 9 is a compare with expected '<', and the bank prints '9. ---', which scripts/render_quick_answers.py reserves for manual-only ids. A grader reading the bank cannot tell a verified relation from an item nobody checked.
evidence: scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt(): the str branch calls sympy.sympify(v), which raises SympifyError on '<' and falls through to the '---' return
render_entry() docstring comment: 'manual-only: the worked solution is the answer' guards the same '---' string

improvements.title: Six explanation prompts are recorded as machine-verified; none is declared manual
improvements.proposed_change: Add a manual entry alongside the existing numeric entry for problems 2, 5, 6, 7, 11 and 12, each with a desc naming what a correct explanation must contain (for 6: 'the index 3 selects the cube table; the square table answers a different question'; for 11: 'a volume formula cubes one length, so it undoes with a cube root'). Enforce it mechanically rather than by instruction: add a check to tests/check_layout.py that scans each \problem body for an explanation imperative ('explain', 'say why', 'state which ... and why', 'in one sentence', 'decide whether ... and explain') and fails when the problem id carries no entry of type manual in the verification JSON. SKILL.md line 257 already states the rule; what is missing is the gate that makes ignoring it impossible.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture worksheet whose problem 1 body reads 'Evaluate $\sqrt{81}$. Explain in one sentence why the answer is not 40.5.' with a verification JSON holding a single eval for id 1, and assert check_layout.py exits non-zero naming problem 1's unflagged explanation. Today it exits 0, which is the defect.
improvements.expected_impact: This sheet moves from '12 verified, 0 manual' to '12 verified, 6 manual', which is the honest report and the one a grader can act on. Across the run this is the second-largest systemic finding (36 cases), and a lint is the only thing that will hold, since SKILL.md already says the right thing and was talked past here.
improvements.risk: Medium. An imperative-verb scan will over-fire on directions prose and on stems that say 'explain your method' as a study habit rather than a graded response. Land it warn-only for one run, tune the phrase list against this corpus, then promote it to a hard gate.

improvements.title: Multi-part problems 1, 5 and 12 print more answer slots than their single verify entry covers
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule from 'one check per problem id' to 'one check per printed response slot'. For this sheet that means: id 1 gains an entry for the factor pair; id 5 gains entries for the bracketing squares (49, 64) and the whole-number bounds (7, 8) from part (a); id 12 gains the same for (64, 125) and (4, 5). The schema already accepts several entries per id -- curr-238 and curr-225 in this same shard do exactly this -- so no format change is needed. Enforce it by having tests/check_layout.py count response macros and \item-labelled subparts inside each \problem segment and fail when that count exceeds the number of verify entries carrying that id.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture problem with three \item subparts (a)(b)(c) against a verification JSON with one entry for that id; assert check_layout.py exits non-zero and names the two uncovered subparts. It passes today.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores checking of the bracketing step, which is the actual skill in the 'estimate-nonperfect-root' facet -- knowing 49 < 60 < 64 is the method, and 7.75 is only its output. This is the dominant systemic finding of the run (61 cases).
improvements.risk: Medium. Counting response macros will initially fire on decorative underlines and on stems that print a worked expansion (as curr-206's problem 1 does). Warn-only first, then gate.

improvements.title: Quick Answers prints an em dash for the verified '<' in problem 9
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, add a relation branch to _fmt() ahead of the sympify attempt that maps the bare tokens '>', '<', '>=', '<=', '=', '≥' and '≤' to their math-mode LaTeX ($>$, $<$, $\ge$, $\le$, $=$) and returns it. Everything else keeps its behaviour, so genuinely manual ids still print '---' and stay distinguishable from a verified relation.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py rendering {"id": 1, "type": "compare", "values": ["sqrt(50)", "7.1"], "order": "relation", "expected": "<"} beside {"id": 2, "type": "manual"}, asserting the bank line for id 1 contains '$<$' and the line for id 2 is '---'. Both render '---' today; I confirmed it by calling render_entry directly.
improvements.expected_impact: The grader's at-a-glance column stops under-reporting what was verified. In this shard it also affects curr-206 (the '=' at problem 9) and curr-232 (both relations at problems 8 and 11).
improvements.risk: Low and contained to the bank, which check_answer_key.py never reads. The only failure mode is a LaTeX spelling that does not compile, which the compile-ak gate catches on the same run.

case_summary: The root mathematics, the facet interleave and the study guide are all strong -- twelve values recomputed clean, four facets rotated so no skeleton repeats, and a reference table that makes problem 3's factoring route ($225 = 9 \times 25$) discoverable. The rejection is the run's dominant defect in a compound form. Six problems (2, 5c, 6, 7, 11, 12c) ask for a written explanation and none is declared manual, while final_response.md states the opposite and invents a 'teaching prose, not separate answers' exemption that SKILL.md line 257 does not grant -- and undercounts them as three. Separately, the bracketing work in 5(a) and 12(a) is exactly machine-checkable (49, 64, 7, 8 and 64, 125, 4, 5) and appears nowhere in verify.json, so the estimation facet's actual method is unchecked while only its rounded output is. One defect the judge did not raise: the bank prints '9. ---' for the verified '<', the same glyph it reserves for unchecked items.
